title: Relaxed Bounds Quarter-Wave Seeded Nelder-Mead
scientific_hypothesis: The score regression from 0.6203 to 0.4402 resulted from premature bound clipping in the gradient-based optimizer; relaxing thickness bounds by ±15% and initializing at quarter-wave positions with a derivative-free Nelder-Mead sampler will recover search space accessibility and improve target score.
design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness at the spectral transition (~700nm) provides a physically motivated starting point; Nelder-Mead avoids gradient-induced local trapping in the widened search volume.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Cr | HfO2 | Al substrate (9 finite layers)
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds [25, 285] nm accommodate ±15% relaxation from prior [30, 250] nm
theory_basis: Admittance locus method for metal-dielectric multilayer optimization
Quarter-wave stack theory for spectral transition positioning
expected_advantages: Wider search space avoids bound-induced local optima
Quarter-wave initialization reduces random search overhead
Nelder-Mead handles non-smooth objective landscapes better than gradient methods
known_risks: Wider bounds may increase optimizer iterations before convergence
Nelder-Mead may converge slower than gradient methods in smooth regions
execution_request_english: Optimize a 9-layer planar multilayer stack on aluminum substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, Cr, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, Cr, HfO2. All layer thicknesses are design variables with bounds [25, 285] nm. Initialize the seed population at quarter-wave optical thickness estimates for 700nm central wavelength: Layer 0 (HfO2) = 135 nm, Layer 1 (SiO2) = 75 nm, Layer 2 (Cr) = 105 nm, Layer 3 (HfO2) = 190 nm, Layer 4 (SiO2) = 75 nm, Layer 5 (HfO2) = 194 nm, Layer 6 (SiO2) = 180 nm, Layer 7 (Cr) = 179 nm, Layer 8 (HfO2) = 148 nm. Use Nelder-Mead derivative-free optimizer. Score candidates by weighted sum: maximize absorptance in 400-700nm band, maximize reflectance in 700-2000nm band. Assume normal incidence, unpolarized light. Evaluate spectral performance across both wavelength bands. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Directly implements feedback directives: relax thickness bounds by ±15%, initialize with quarter-wave estimates at 700nm, switch from gradient_thickness to Nelder-Mead optimizer to avoid premature bound clipping that caused score regression.
